Why my sourdough stopped rising in winter

12 January 2026

Every winter my starter sulks. It bubbles a little, smells fine, and then my loaves come out flat and dense. This year I finally measured what was going on instead of blaming the flour.

The kitchen sits at about 16 °C at night. At that temperature the yeast and bacteria in the starter work at maybe half their summer pace, so a feeding schedule that worked in July leaves the starter underfed and sour by the time I bake.

The fix was boring: feed it with warm water, keep the jar on top of the fridge, and wait for it to double before mixing the dough. I wrote myself a tiny script to remind me how long to wait:

def hours_to_double(temp_c):
    # roughly halves for every 8 degrees warmer
    return 4 * 2 ** ((24 - temp_c) / 8)

print(round(hours_to_double(16), 1))

Six and a half hours at sixteen degrees sounds about right, and the last three loaves have risen properly. Next I want to try a stiffer starter, which is said to cope better with the cold.
